newsitem.title: USA: CME details butter futures/cash contract changes.
newsitem.headline: CME details butter futures/cash contract changes.

text.p: The Chicago Mercantile Exchange said chnages in contract terms for CME butter futures and the spot butter market will take effect on Friday, August 15.
The changes were approved by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission on August 8.

A new CME butter contract cycle of February, March, May, July, September and October futures will be established with February through July 1998 contracts to be listed on Friday, according to a report issued by the CME on Thursday.
Previous trading months were February, April, June, July, September and November.
The weight range for deliveries will increase to 40,000 to 43,000 lbs from 40,000 to 42,000 lbs.

Position limits in the expiring contract month at the close of business on the first business day following the first Friday of the contract month will be 150 contracts depending on the contract month, the CME said.

Only grade AA butter produced on or after November 1 of a given year will be deliverable until October 31 of the next year. A provision that the U.S. Agriculture Department grading cerfificate included in the delivery documents must be no more than six months old will be eliminated.
Current delivery requirements now key on the production date, a CME spokesman said.
An increase in the age of butter deliverable into the spot call contract was also approved and takes effect on August 15.
Stored butter may not be delivered if the day of sale is later than the 10th business day of the 12th month after the month of manufacture of the earliest churning in the carlot.

The requirement had been the first business day of the seventh month and the change was made to make it easier for traders to buy spot butter to fill deliveries or sell delivered butter in the spot, the CME said.
